title: Nebraska: 1984 Orange Bowl
description: A fumblerooski, a backup I-back's late score, and a tipped two-point pass—Go Deep into the night that still haunts Lincoln.

questions.question: Trailing Miami late in the 1984 Orange Bowl, which backup I-back—in for the injured Heisman winner—scored from 24 yards to make it 31–30?
questions.explanation: The Heisman winner had left with a badly bruised ankle. Smith already had a 1-yard TD earlier in the fourth; the 24-yarder on fourth-and-eight with 48 seconds left set up the call Lincoln still argues about.

questions.question: After Jeff Smith's TD made it 31–30, Nebraska skipped the tying kick and went for what?
questions.explanation: A kick ties it and almost certainly locks a shared national title. Tom Osborne went for the win instead—the only time his name needs to appear in this stack. The pass never connected.

questions.question: Whose two-point conversion pass—intended for Jeff Smith—did Miami's Kenny Calhoun tip away to seal 31–30?
questions.explanation: Gill rolled and fired; Calhoun got a hand on it. Final: Miami 31, Nebraska 30. Bernie Kosar had thrown for 300 yards earlier. Lincoln still finishes the sentence for you.

questions.question: Earlier that same Orange Bowl, before Gill's tipped pass, which Outland Trophy guard scored on the "Fumblerooski"?
questions.explanation: Third-and-five at the Miami 19: Gill "fumbles" the snap to the turf, Steinkuhler scoops left and runs 19 yards. It worked. The two-point try later that night still didn't.

questions.question: Steinkuhler's fumblerooski came after which Heisman Trophy I-back—Nebraska's engine—left the Orange Bowl with a bruised ankle?
questions.explanation: Rozier was the 1983 Heisman winner. When he went out in the third quarter, Smith became the night's unlikely closer—and the two-point debate's permanent supporting character.

deeperMode.title: Go Deeper: After the Heartbreak
deeperMode.description: How the dynasty answered Miami years later

questions.question: Which Nebraska quarterback ran the option through the 1994–95 title seasons and the Fiesta Bowl wrecking of Florida?
questions.hint: His 75-yard option TD in the '96 Fiesta Bowl is the signature clip

questions.question: In that 1996 Fiesta Bowl (1995 season), Nebraska beat Florida by what final score?
questions.hint: Steve Spurrier's Fun 'n' Gun met option football at full speed

easterEgg.title: Kenny Calhoun's fingertips
easterEgg.text: Calhoun tipped Gill's pass bound for Jeff Smith. Miami's first national title. Nebraska's open wound. Fans can still diagram the play in the air with two fingers.
